properties.name: Withlacoochee River PUD
properties.utilities: No public water / no public sewer reported
properties.summary: Rare riverfront acreage with advertised PUD zoning and strong Old Florida recreational appeal. Legal access, buildable acreage, utilities, and the controlling PUD documents decide whether it can become a clean destination fish camp or merely very attractive wet dirt.

confirmed: Asking price is within the $500,000 land budget.
Listing reports 9.63 acres and substantial Withlacoochee River frontage.
The location has strong fishing, boating, and Old Florida destination appeal.
unknowns: What uses are actually authorized by the controlling PUD documents?
How many acres remain buildable after floodplain, wetlands, buffers, and stormwater?
Can commercial water and wastewater needs be met economically?
Is the existing access legally sufficient for a commercial RV destination?
dealKillers: RV or campground use is prohibited by the PUD or future land-use designation.
Environmental constraints leave too little usable acreage for a viable first phase.
Commercial access cannot be permitted or legally secured.
Water and wastewater costs overwhelm the site's revenue potential.
nextActions: Request the controlling PUD ordinance and written use determination from Marion County.
Confirm parcel ID, legal access, and commercial entrance requirements.
Order a desktop wetlands, floodplain, and buildable-acreage review.

properties.name: Improved 40-Acre Retreat
properties.locationAccuracy: Approximate marker pending parcel GIS verification
properties.utilities: Well, septic, electric, and one RV hookup reported
properties.summary: Large, inexpensive tract with existing well, septic, electric, pole barn, bathhouse, and RV hookup. It lacks a confirmed natural destination draw, but it offers one of the cheapest phased-start platforms currently in the queue.

confirmed: The asking price leaves substantially more capital for phased construction.
The listing reports existing well, septic, electric, bathhouse, pole barn, and an RV hookup.
Forty acres provides strong expansion and layout flexibility.
unknowns: Is commercial RV or campground use permitted or realistically approvable?
How much of the tract is suitable for roads, pads, stormwater, and wastewater?
Can the existing private utilities contribute to commercial development?
What experience would make guests choose this location rather than merely pass through?
dealKillers: County policy makes commercial campground approval unrealistic.
Soils, wetlands, or floodplain make commercial wastewater or site development impractical.
The surrounding demand cannot support a destination-oriented operation.
nextActions: Verify parcel zoning, future land use, and campground approval path with Madison County.
Review flood, wetlands, soils, and usable acreage using county and environmental tools.
Determine the capacity and legal status of the existing well, septic, electric, and RV hookup.

properties.name: 40-Acre Mini Farm near I-10
properties.locationAccuracy: Approximate marker pending parcel GIS verification
properties.floodZone: Unknown; pond and lowland review required
properties.utilities: Residence and farm utilities present; commercial capacity unknown
properties.summary: Forty acres with mature oaks, pasture, ponds, an existing residence, and proximity to Madison and I-10. It has character and operational head-start potential, but the ponds, transmission corridor, easements, and commercial entitlement path need scrutiny.

confirmed: The tract is large enough for meaningful phased development.
The listing reports an existing residence, pasture, mature oaks, and multiple ponds.
Proximity to Madison and I-10 could simplify supplies, staffing, and regional access.
unknowns: Are the ponds amenities, environmental constraints, or both?
What impacts do the transmission corridor and reported easements have on the site plan?
Can the road safely and legally support large-RV commercial traffic?
Is there enough nearby recreation and demand to create a memorable destination?
dealKillers: Ponds, wetlands, easements, and utility corridors fragment the usable acreage beyond practicality.
Commercial RV access cannot be safely permitted.
The county will not support the intended transient use.
nextActions: Pull the parcel, zoning, future land use, easements, and utility-corridor information.
Map floodplain, wetlands, ponds, and likely usable development areas.
Ask Madison County about campground use and commercial entrance requirements.

properties.name: 47-Acre Multi-Use Farm
properties.locationAccuracy: Approximate marker pending parcel GIS verification
properties.floodZone: Advertised high and dry; independent verification required
properties.summary: The largest tract in the current queue, advertised as high and dry with irrigated acreage and existing improvements. Strong expansion flexibility, but it needs a compelling destination story and a verified entitlement path before it outranks waterfront or recreation-driven sites.

confirmed: This is the largest current candidate at approximately 47 acres.
The listing reports existing residential and agricultural improvements plus irrigated acreage.
The asking price remains within budget and has been reduced.
unknowns: Is the advertised high-and-dry condition supported by official mapping and field conditions?
Can existing agricultural infrastructure reduce first-phase development costs?
Will Madison County support commercial campground or RV-destination use?
What compelling guest experience can the property provide without expensive manufactured amenities?
dealKillers: The entitlement path is politically or technically unrealistic.
The site lacks enough natural or regional draw to sustain the intended business.
Commercial utilities and wastewater require disproportionate investment.
nextActions: Verify zoning, future land use, and campground approval path with Madison County.
Independently check floodplain, wetlands, soils, and the high-and-dry claim.
Inventory existing infrastructure and identify the strongest feasible destination concept.
